preamble: Insertion of the open-mid front vowel [ɛ] is the defining change of the Hebrew segolate nouns. Proto-Semitic monosyllables ending in two consonants, such as *malk 'king', had the final cluster broken by an anaptyctic vowel. In the Tiberian reading tradition that vowel is segol [ɛ], giving mɛ́lɛḵ. The original cluster comes back before suffixes, as in malkī 'my king'.

examples.note: Segol [ɛ] is inserted between the final l and k; the stem malk- surfaces before suffixes.
The final cluster -pr is broken by [ɛ]; Modern Hebrew sefer.
The final cluster -rṣ is split by [ɛ]; the stem ʔarṣ- surfaces before suffixes.
